page: MVC pattern best practices with Elysia. Pattern-agnostic framework allowing flexible coding patterns. Difficulty decoupling and handling types with MVC. Feature-based folder structure recommendation. Code organization: modules, utils, features. Controller, Service, Model separation. Controllers handle HTTP routing and validation. Services handle business logic decoupled from HTTP. Models define data structure and validation. TypeScript types with UnwrapSchema. Cookie proxy behavior - never null/undefined. strictNullChecks configuration. Questions: What folder structure should I use? How do I structure MVC with Elysia? How do I decouple business logic from HTTP?

sections.manifest: Feature-based folder structure for Elysia applications. Organize by feature not by layer. auth module, user module organization. Each feature has: index.ts (controller), service.ts, model.ts. src/modules directory structure. src/utils for shared utilities. Keep related code together. Modules self-contained. Questions: How should I organize my Elysia project? What is feature-based structure? How do I structure folders?

Controller patterns in Elysia avoiding tight coupling. Treat Elysia instance as controller itself. One Elysia instance = one controller. Routes defined directly on Elysia instance. Don't pass entire Context to controller methods. Object destructuring to extract needed properties. Decouple controller from HTTP request. Context is highly dynamic type. Controller without HTTP request dependency. Loss of type integrity with Context parameter. Vendor lock-in prevention. Testing without HTTP overhead using handle() method. Bun test integration. Questions: How should I structure controllers? Should I use classes for controllers? How do I test controllers?

Service layer patterns for business logic. Non-request dependent service as static class. Abstract class with static methods to avoid allocation. Request-dependent service as Elysia instance. Macro system for request-dependent patterns. isSignIn macro with resolve. Plugin deduplication by name property. Decorate only request-dependent properties. requestIP, requestTime, session decoration patterns. Avoid overusing decorators for vendor lock-in. Questions: How do I structure services? Should services depend on HTTP context? How do I handle request-dependent logic?

Model and DTO patterns for data validation. Elysia.t validation system as model. Single source of truth for types and validation. t.Object() for object models. UnwrapSchema for extracting TypeScript types. Model grouping into single object. Optional model type extraction. Don't declare class instances as models. Don't declare interfaces separately from validation. Model reference with model() method. Model injection into controllers. Elysia reference model for remap and remapping. OpenAPI model integration. Questions: How do I define models? Should I use classes for models? How do I extract types from validation?
